narrative.intro: Regents of the University of California obligated $1.2B in FY2026 to date, across 3 awards with an average award size of $410M. Obligations fell 5.9% year over year. Fiscal-year history shows obligations of $67.4M in FY21, $6.7M in FY22, $982M in FY23, $1.4B in FY24, and $1.3B in FY25. The Department of Energy is the dominant buyer with $1.2B in obligations in FY2026 to date. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences is the largest market for obligations, at $1.2B, followed by Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools at $4M and Computer Facilities Management Services at $31.3K. Current-year totals are partial because the period is fiscal year to date.

sections.heading: What is Regents of the University of California's federal contracting footprint?
sections.body: Regents of the University of California obligated $1.2B in FY2026 to date. Regents of the University of California recorded 3 awards in the current year with an average award size of $410M. Obligations fell 5.9% year over year. Fiscal-year obligations ranged from $6.7M in FY22 up to $1.4B in FY24.

sections.heading: Who buys from Regents of the University of California and what markets receive the obligations?
sections.body: The Department of Energy bought $1.2B in FY2026 to date. The Department of Commerce bought $31.3K in FY2026 to date. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences received $1.2B in obligations, Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools received $4M, and Computer Facilities Management Services received $31.3K.

faq.q: How much does Regents of the University of California make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California has $1.2B in contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Regents of the University of California recorded 3 awards this fiscal year, with an average award size of $410M, and obligations fell 5.9% year over year.

faq.q: Which agencies buy from Regents of the University of California?
faq.a: The Department of Energy buys from Regents of the University of California and obligated $1.2B in FY2026 to date. The Department of Commerce also bought from Regents of the University of California and obligated $31.3K in FY2026 to date.

faq.q: What does Regents of the University of California sell to the government?
faq.a: Regents of the University of California sells research and related services to the government, with Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences accounting for $1.2B in obligations. Regents of the University of California also delivered work tied to Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools at $4M and Computer Facilities Management Services at $31.3K.

faq.q: Which Regents of the University of California contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: No expiring-contracts figures are listed for Regents of the University of California. The note states that award-value figures in the largest-awards and expiring-contracts tables are total contract values, but no specific expiring-contracts entries are provided.
